title: PageFlex: Flexible and Efficient User-space Delegation of Linux Paging Policies with eBPF
problem: Linux kernel paging policies are rigid and cannot be customized per-application without kernel modifications. Different workloads have varying memory access patterns and page replacement requirements that would benefit from tailored eviction strategies.
motivation: Enabling applications to customize paging policies at runtime allows optimization for diverse memory access patterns and workload-specific performance requirements without kernel changes.
method: PageFlex uses eBPF programs deployed in user-space to intercept kernel paging decisions and apply custom page selection and eviction logic. The framework hooks into kernel memory reclamation events, allowing user-space handlers to override or influence page victim selection based on application-defined criteria while maintaining kernel safety via eBPF verification.
key_novelty: Leveraging eBPF to safely delegate Linux kernel paging policy decisions to user-space applications, enabling runtime customization and per-workload memory management optimization without kernel modifications.
contributions: eBPF-based framework for user-space delegation of paging policy decisions
Safe mechanism to intercept and modify kernel page victim selection at runtime
Flexible policy abstraction allowing diverse custom memory management strategies

metrics.other: Memory efficiency and page fault reduction

primary_theme: User-space customizable memory paging via eBPF
